macros.name: articlesecuritylabel
macros.doc: Use this to label documents of class article.

macros.name: booksecuritylabel
macros.doc: Use this one to label books.

macros.name: bydefault
macros.doc: Use the \bydefault tag to talk about how a product we use implements a given requirement in its default configuration.

macros.name: distributionA
macros.doc: To mark your document with Distro A (public release), write \distributionA {⟨other information⟩}.

macros.name: distributionD
macros.doc: Use this macro to indicate that your document uses Distribution Statement D, and why, like so: \distributionD {⟨reason why distribution is limited⟩}.

macros.name: documents
macros.doc: Use \documents for notating some text in your document that says a fact about a system which supports a requirement.

macros.name: doneby
macros.doc: The \doneby tag is for requirements that are not fulfilled in an automated fashion: people are responsible for carrying them out on a day-by-day basis.

macros.name: implements
macros.doc: The \implements tag notates a section of code or documentation which directly implements a requirement.

macros.name: makedodtitle
macros.doc: Just like you need \maketitle to make your \title show up, you need to (instead) use \makedodtitle to make your distribution statement show up.

macros.name: requirement
macros.doc: Use this macro to mention requirements that come from other documents, without implying a particular compliance posture.

macros.name: unimplemented
macros.doc: Use the \unimplemented tag to talk about a requirement we need to fulfill but haven’t yet.

macros.name: version
macros.doc: Use the \version {⟨some indication of version⟩} to indicate the version of the document.
